summary: Halyard mutual NDA with Dutch counterparty edits that widen the Purpose, narrow the carve-outs (deleting independent development), add a 24-month non-solicit, and request a shorter survival period and Dutch law.

findings.quote: VLIET & VAN DER BERG ADVIES B.V., a private company with limited liability
findings.why: Counterparty placeholders were completed with Dutch entity details (RQ07), which the lawyer should confirm against the Dutch Trade Register.

findings.quote: each Party may disclose certain Confidential Information to the other Party
findings.why: Disclosing Party and Receiving Party are defined by role, so obligations bind both parties equally.

findings.quote: potential commercial opportunities, strategic evaluations, advisory engagements, and any other internal or external business activities of the respective Parties from time to time
findings.why: The inserted Purpose is open-ended ('any other internal or external business activities') rather than discussions about a potential commercial relationship.
findings.draft_redline: The Parties wish to enter into discussions regarding a potential commercial relationship between them (the Purpose).
findings.note_to_counterparty: We have kept the Purpose limited to discussions about a potential commercial relationship so that both parties' information is used only for that. We are happy to name a specific project if that helps.

findings.quote: either marked or identified as confidential at the time of disclosure or would reasonably be considered confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of its disclosure
findings.why: Definition covers information disclosed for the Purpose that is marked or reasonably confidential and includes derived notes and analyses, for either party.

findings.quote: [[INS: (including, in respect of the Counterparty, any groepsmaatschappij within the meaning of Article 2:24b of the Dutch Civil Code)]]
findings.why: The Group definition is widened only for the Counterparty by reference to a Dutch law concept that may capture entities beyond subsidiaries and holding companies, so the playbook does not clearly cover it.
findings.draft_redline: Delete the inserted wording so that Group has the same meaning for both Parties.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would prefer the Group definition to apply identically to both parties. The existing wording already covers your subsidiaries and holding companies.

findings.quote: [[INS: or for its internal business assessment, service benchmarking and market evaluation]]
findings.why: The deletion of 'solely' and the insert allow use for the Receiving Party's own internal business assessment, benchmarking and market evaluation, beyond the Purpose.
findings.draft_redline: 2.1.2 not use or exploit the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information in any way except solely for the Purpose;
findings.note_to_counterparty: We need use of Confidential Information to be limited solely to the Purpose. Benchmarking and market evaluation are not something we can agree to for either party.

findings.quote: not reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble or otherwise attempt to derive the composition, source code or underlying structure
findings.why: The reverse engineering prohibition is retained unchanged.

findings.quote: [[INS: contemporaneous documentary]]
findings.why: The evidence standard is raised from 'written records or other reasonable evidence' to 'contemporaneous documentary' evidence, which narrows the carve-outs.
findings.draft_redline: which the Receiving Party can demonstrate by written records or other reasonable evidence:
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would like to keep the evidence standard as 'written records or other reasonable evidence', which works equally for both parties.

findings.quote: [[INS: as evidenced by the Receiving Party's written records dated prior to the date of this Agreement]]
findings.why: The already-lawfully-held carve-out is narrowed because it now depends on written records dated before the Agreement.
findings.draft_redline: was already lawfully in the possession of the Receiving Party prior to its disclosure by or on behalf of the Disclosing Party, free from any restriction as to its use or disclosure;
findings.note_to_counterparty: We think the general evidence wording in clause 3.1 is sufficient, so we would prefer not to add a separate dated-records requirement.

findings.quote: [[DEL: 3.1.4 is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to, use of, or reference to any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.]]
findings.why: The independent development carve-out is deleted, leaving only three of the four standard exceptions.
findings.draft_redline: 3.1.4 is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to, use of, or reference to any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
findings.note_to_counterparty: The independent development exception is standard and protects both parties, so we have reinstated it.

findings.quote: who strictly need to know such Confidential Information in order to evaluate or further the Purpose
findings.why: Disclosure to Representatives (employees, officers, directors, advisers, auditors, insurers) and Group members is allowed on a need-to-know basis with the Receiving Party liable for them.

findings.quote: to the extent that it is legally permitted to do so
findings.why: Compelled disclosure is permitted, with notice and cooperation only where legally permitted and resistance at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: within ten Business Days of receipt of such request
findings.why: Return or destruction within 10 Business Days with officer-signed confirmation and a backup and legal-retention exception in 6.2 that stays confidential under 6.3.

findings.quote: shall remain the exclusive property of the Disclosing Party (or its licensors, as applicable)
findings.why: Confidential Information and IP stay with the Disclosing Party and 7.2 grants no licence beyond use for the Purpose.

findings.quote: Neither Party makes any representation or gives any warranty, express or implied, as to the accuracy, completeness, adequacy or fitness for a particular purpose
findings.why: Mutual as-is and no-warranty disclaimer, with 7.5 confirming no obligation to proceed.

findings.quote: nothing in this Agreement shall operate or be construed so as to exclude, restrict or limit the liability of either Party in respect of fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation
findings.why: The rewrite is wordier but still disclaims reliance liability for both parties and keeps the fraud carve-out.
findings.fallback_cited: Mutual disclaimers in any reasonable wording.

findings.quote: without the prior written consent of the other Party, except as required by law or any governmental or regulatory authority in accordance with Clause 5
findings.why: Mutual publicity restriction with a legal-requirement exception.

findings.quote: that Party shall not disclose such personal data unless and until the Parties have agreed and entered into a separate written data processing agreement or data sharing agreement
findings.why: Personal data is limited to business contact details and any further sharing requires a separate DPA or data sharing agreement first.

findings.quote: for a period of two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice
findings.why: Two-year term with 30 days' notice to terminate early, as preferred.

findings.quote: for a period of three (3) years from the effective date of expiry or termination
findings.why: Confidentiality survives three years after expiry or termination, with Trade Secrets protected while they remain Trade Secrets.

findings.quote: Our internal policy caps post-termination confidentiality obligations at 18 months from the date of disclosure.
findings.why: The comment asks for survival of 18 months from disclosure, which is below the 2-year minimum acceptable survival and so needs escalation under RQ01.
findings.draft_redline: Keep clause 10.3 as drafted (three years from expiry or termination, with Trade Secrets protected while they remain Trade Secrets).
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are unable to reduce survival to 18 months from disclosure. We could consider a shorter period of no less than two years after expiry or termination, keeping indefinite protection for Trade Secrets.

findings.quote: [[INS: 1.1.9 Key Personnel means any director, officer, partner, consultant, software engineer or senior employee of a Party or any member of its Group with whom the other Party or any member of its Group comes into contact or about whom it receives information in connection with the Purpose.]]
findings.why: The new Key Personnel definition feeds the non-solicit and reaches consultants and Group staff, going beyond staff the party worked with in the discussions.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We do not think a non-solicitation covenant is needed in a short-form NDA, so we have removed the related definition.

findings.quote: neither Party shall, and each Party shall procure that no member of its Group shall, without the prior written consent of the other Party, directly or indirectly solicit, entice away, offer employment to, engage or employ any Key Personnel
findings.why: The new non-solicit runs for the term plus 24 months, bars hiring as well as soliciting, binds Group members and has no general-advertising exception, exceeding the PB15 fallback limits.
findings.note_to_counterparty: Thank you for the proposed mutual non-solicit. We are not able to include it, as the NDA is intended only to protect confidential information and does not restrict hiring.

findings.quote: a Party shall be entitled to seek the remedies of injunction, specific performance and other equitable relief
findings.why: Mutual right to seek equitable relief and 11.2 keeps remedies cumulative.

findings.quote: without the prior written consent of the other Party
findings.why: Neither Party may assign or deal with its rights without prior written consent.

findings.quote: our standard position is for Dutch law and the District Court of Amsterdam (Rechtbank Amsterdam) to apply under Clauses 12.10 and 12.11
findings.why: The comment asks for Dutch governing law and Amsterdam courts (RQ03); the clause text itself remains English law, so the request must be declined or escalated.
findings.draft_redline: Keep clauses 12.10 and 12.11 as drafted; if a concession is needed, English law with non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are not able to move to Dutch law, but we are happy to keep English law and could consider non-exclusive jurisdiction of the English courts.

findings.quote: the courts of England and Wales shall have exclusive jurisdiction
findings.why: English law and exclusive English jurisdiction as preferred.
